life_summary: Henry Dinwoodey Moyle was born on April 22, 1889, in Salt Lake City, Utah Territory. He grew up in the urban center of the LDS Church and received his education in Salt Lake Valley schools. Moyle married Clara Alberta Wright on a date in the early twentieth century at the Salt Lake Temple, and together they had six children. He established himself as a respected community and Church figure, bringing professional acumen to ecclesiastical responsibilities. His career spanned the transformative decades of the twentieth century, from the early years after statehood through the post-World War II era. Moyle's life was characterized by a willingness to experiment with innovative approaches to Church growth and membership engagement.
church_summary: Moyle served as a missionary in Switzerland and Germany during his youth. He was ordained to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 1947 and served in that capacity until his death in 1963. During his apostolic ministry, Moyle became known for implementing innovative but ultimately controversial initiatives aimed at increasing Church membership and engagement. Most notably, he developed the baseball baptism program, designed to attract converts through athletic engagement, though this approach was largely opposed by other apostles and proved unsuccessful in retaining active members. Despite the mixed reception of some initiatives, Moyle remained committed to the task of strengthening the Church.
